page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, it features an AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, corresponding to 4 vCPUs. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB total, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The cache structure consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. It lacks integrated local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage while offering an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark measurements position the m8gb.xlarge predominantly in the mid-range across core compute and memory evaluation suites. Geekbench multi-core testing reached 5,967.0, accompanied by a clang compilation score of 8,694.0 and stress-ng multi-core output of 6,816.76. Memory bandwidth is consistent with modern DDR subsystems, achieving 96.54 GB/sec on uncached reads. Decompression performance shows particular strength, with single-threaded bzip3 decompression measuring 14.41 GB/sec. However, synthetic PassMark CPU scores fell into lower quartiles, notably in encryption throughput, and small-model prompt processing scored within the bottom 25%.

With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated physical execution threads, the instance delivers predictable general-purpose compute capacity. Its qualitative cost efficiency derives from running efficient ARM-based hardware without paying for idle local storage or specialized accelerators. This profile makes the instance appropriate for containerized web applications, microservices, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD runners, and routine relational or transactional database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 4-core AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of system memory, and an 8 Gbps baseline network link, it functions on the Nitro hypervisor without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In synthetic and application benchmarks, it demonstrates solid mid-tier execution across Geekbench compilation, stress-ng workloads, and static web serving, supplemented by strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression results. Specialized cryptographic and PassMark scores remain lower relative to x86 peers. With 4.0 GB of memory per core and no unneeded peripheral overhead, the instance provides balanced resource utilization for containerized microservices, web servers, build pipelines, and caching layers.
